candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: boundaries (practice guide 40, supplement 3)
verified_facts: A legal boundary is an exact imaginary line and is rarely identified precisely on the ground or in conveyances.
The legal boundary is not shown on Ordnance Survey mapping.
A visible fence, wall or hedge may or may not coincide with the legal boundary.
semantic_limits: Physical features and OS mapping cannot be treated as exact legal-boundary evidence for parcel geometry.

candidates.name: Boundary agreements and determined boundaries (practice guide 40, supplement 4)
verified_facts: General boundaries remain general unless determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
A determined boundary shows the exact line of the boundary for the register.
Where measurements are used on a determined-boundary plan they must be accurate to +/-10mm and taken horizontally from defined permanent features.
semantic_limits: INSPIRE or ordinary title-plan geometry cannot be promoted to determined-boundary legal precision without the required register evidence.
